title: Risk profiling: capacity, tolerance and need
objectives: Tell risk capacity, tolerance and need apart.
Apply the rule: match the lower of capacity and tolerance.
body_md:
| Dimension | What it measures | How to assess |
|---|---|---|
| Risk capacity | How much loss the client can afford | Age, income stability, dependants, existing assets, horizon |
| Risk tolerance | How much loss the client can stomach | Past reactions to market falls, comfort questions, questionnaire |
| Risk need | How much risk the goal actually requires | Goal amount vs current savings and time left |

Match recommendations to the lower of capacity and tolerance. Re-profile after major life events.
example: A business owner earns well, has no debt and a 15-year horizon, so his capacity is high. But he sold everything in March 2020, so his tolerance is low. He is profiled as Moderate, not Aggressive.
say: A wealthy client who panics in falls is still a moderate investor. Let's build for how you will actually react.
Let's re-profile now that your circumstances have changed.
never: You can afford the risk, so you should take it.
The questionnaire says Aggressive, so that is what you are.

check.q: A wealthy client with high risk capacity panics and sells in every market fall. How should they be profiled?
o: Moderate: match to the lower of capacity and tolerance
Aggressive, to make up for past losses
check.why: Recommendations follow the LOWER of capacity and tolerance. Low tolerance sets the limit.

check.q: "How much risk the goal actually requires" describes:
check.why: Risk need compares the goal amount with current savings and time left.

check.q: When should a client's risk profile be reviewed again?
o: Never, it is fixed at onboarding
check.why: Re-profile after major life events such as a job change, marriage or retirement.
